title: Private VPC Quarterly Sprint Matrix and Activation Runway
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: produce a sprint-by-sprint plan (sprint matrix) that operationalizes the Private/VPC activation runway for Q2 2026. This ticket synthesizes dependencies across runtime, ops, console, billing, and security to produce an actionable activation playbook and a gated rollout sequence for early adopter cohorts.

Scope: tenant onboarding UX (console + CLI), per-tenant KMS key integration, controlled runtime upgrade orchestration (canary + progressive), dedicated capacity autoscaling flags, billing reconciliation signals, and preflight compatibility checks for common on-prem topologies. Excludes full multi-region replication and offline air-gapped packaging (those are separate epics).

Success metrics: 1) 3 pilot tenants onboarded in Q2 with no P1 incidents; 2) activation time for a tenant (from contract to first inference) < 10 business days for default path; 3) runtime upgrade mean time to rollback < 15 minutes in canary waves; 4) console activation flow conversion >= 80% in pilot cohort.

Deliverables: sprint matrix (detailed tasks per 2-week sprint), gating checklist for each rollout wave, automated smoke/regression job matrix, a customer-facing activation runbook, and a post-pilot lessons doc.

Trade-offs considered: prioritize reliability & security for pilot tenants over speed-to-activate for broad self-serve; this increases manual runway but reduces P1 risk. Proposed approach uses conservative default (managed KMS integration and preflight compatibility checks) with an early-availability fast-path for low-risk tenants.

Stakeholders: Product (Ava Martinez), Runtime (Nina Park), Infra/Autoscaling (Luis Ortega), Security & Compliance (Maya Patel), Console UX (Jon Reynolds), Billing (Priya Desai), Solutions Eng (Marco Ruiz).
